name: Advanced Land Imager on Earth Observing-1
description: MIT Lincoln Laboratory's Advanced Land Imager demonstrated a pushbroom sensor in orbit aboard NASA's Earth Observing-1. A line of detectors measured along a swath as the spacecraft moved, producing multispectral and panchromatic views for comparison with Landsat.

date.label: 21 November 2000
date.basis: The instrument developer reports the launch date, site and payload.

events.statement: NASA launched Earth Observing-1 carrying the Advanced Land Imager from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California.

evidence.supports: Dates the launch and identifies ALI aboard the spacecraft.

date.label: 25 November 2000
date.basis: Lincoln Laboratory dates the inaugural image acquisition to 25 November.

events.statement: The Advanced Land Imager collected its first Earth scenes, including a panchromatic scene of Sutton, Alaska.

evidence.supports: Identifies the acquisition day and the Sutton image.
Confirms successful Alaska imaging and comparison of the panchromatic observations to Landsat 7.

date.basis: MIT Lincoln Laboratory reports the spacecraft's retirement in 2017. USGS documents a wind-down in stages.

events.statement: EO-1 operations ended in 2017. The historical Advanced Land Imager scenes remained available from the USGS archive.

evidence.supports: Records the end of normal imaging and continued access to archived data.

earliest_record.rationale: The first dated milestone retained here is the launch of the integrated instrument. Its first on-orbit observations are recorded separately.
